findings.summary: ROUND 1 — the schema-walking Brake's central claim ('a composite added later is covered the day it is declared') was FALSE. Coverage was gated on the hand-written FIXTURE, not the schema: a composite absent from the fixture makes baseline and corrupted runs collapse to the same .catch() default, so before===after trivially. The reviewer added a fifth composite carrying the exact #303 bug — both generated cases PASSED — and extending the guard-the-guard name list gave 14/14 GREEN WITH THE BUG SHIPPED. Superseded by the operator's SPLIT ruling: the schema-walking guard is withdrawn from this PR entirely (see R3-VERDICT), so this finding no longer applies to the shipped code.

ROUND 1 — provenance.origin was a dead case: the poison value was a Symbol, which z.unknown() ACCEPTS, so it could never fail; origin was also absent from the fixture, so it was never checked as a victim either. 11 reported cases, 10 real. Withdrawn with the walker.

ROUND 1 — A FALSE CAUSAL CLAIM, and the most important finding in the review. The author claimed a bad refs.supersedes erases the ADR-0004 supersession edge consumed at engine.ts:333, resurrecting a superseded decision. MEASURED FALSE: refs.contradicts already carried its own .catch(undefined) pre-fix (src/validate.ts:44, an unchanged context line), so the cited input never detonated refs at all; and the only input that loses supersedes is a malformed supersedes ITSELF, where no valid edge ever existed and whose behaviour is unchanged by the fix. THE ADR-0004 LIFECYCLE BYPASS IS NOT REACHABLE. The suite had agreed all along and was misread: the sole refs failure was contradicts destroyed by a bad supersedes — the opposite direction. Corrected in the test header, on #303 (comment 5675774505) and in the PR body; the first commit body is immutable. The real refs win is smaller and is what the shipped test asserts: contradicts survives (cli.ts:567).
ROUND 1 — nested composites were invisible to the walker. Withdrawn with the walker.

ROUND 2 — CATCH DEFAULT EQUALS FIXTURE VALUE. If a composite's .catch() default matches the fixture, every sibling comparison compares the default with ITSELF; the object detonates and the test cannot see it. Observed 15/15 green with the bug. Not hypothetical for the live schema — had wellFormed().author.role been 'executor' (the author catch default at src/validate.ts:40) that composite would already have been vacuous. Withdrawn with the walker.

ROUND 2 — INVALID FIXTURE VALUE PRE-DETONATES THE BASELINE, and this is the answer to a question round 1 asked and the author answered WRONGLY. Asked whether 'if (before[sibling] === undefined) continue' was still a silent skip, the author claimed STRUCTURAL 1 made it unreachable. It did not: STRUCTURAL 1 inspects the RAW fixture and never the PARSED baseline, so a field given '3' instead of 3 makes the baseline collapse to the catch default, every sibling hits the continue, and expect(baseline.ok).toBe(true) still passes because the catch rescues it — 15/15 green with NO field carrying a catch at all. Withdrawn with the walker.

ROUND 2 — ARRAY- AND UNION-REACHABLE COMPOSITES were invisible to the walker AND to both structural assertions: no cases generated, no complaint, no signal of any kind. Strictly worse than the pre-fix state of R1-B1, which at least tripped the guard-the-guard. Withdrawn with the walker.

ROUND 2 — the UNCORRUPTIBLE exemption claimed a field 'accepts EVERY value' while testing exactly one (the Symbol), and its own error message offered 'poison it differently' when no per-field override existed — so the exemption was the only workable response, granting a standing zero-coverage pass under a false reason. Withdrawn with the walker.

ROUND 3 — FALSE POSITIVE INTRODUCED BY ROUND 2'S OWN FIX, which is the ADR-0070 §4 distress signal and the reason this was escalated to the operator rather than iterated a fourth time. A new composite written with plain z.object — zod's default idiom — with correct per-field catches and NO bug went RED claiming "object-level .catch() ALREADY fired ... one of its values is invalid". Nothing had fired: z.object STRIPS the undeclared sentinel that round 2's fix relied on, and the sentinel cannot distinguish 'stripped by a strict schema' from 'object detonated'. NO HONEST FIX EXISTS — a stripping object cannot preserve an undeclared key — leaving a developer only the choice of changing production code to satisfy a test or gutting the assertion. z.strictObject and z.object().catchall() fail identically, and all three have _def.type === 'object', so the completeness check says nothing. A gate that blocks correct work is a defect (ADR-0052). RESOLVED by the operator's SPLIT ruling: the sentinel and the whole schema-walking guard are withdrawn.

ROUND 3 — SIXTH ESCAPE, with a LARGER blast radius than the bug the guard is named after: root-level fields were entirely outside it (the walker skips the root at its own `if (path.length)`). Adding a root field without .catch() left the suite 788/788 GREEN with all three structural assertions silent, while a malformed value produced ok=false and DROPPED THE WHOLE ENTRY from the live set — not merely its siblings. This is the surface where fields actually get added: status, why, constitutional, adr_no and session_id are all root fields added over time and all carry .catch() precisely because it matters. RESOLVED for the shipped code by the split; the replacement structural guard covers root fields for free, which is a principal reason for choosing it.

ROUND 3 — SIXTH ESCAPE (b): an object-level .catch(ctx => ctx.value) with no per-field catches — the literal definition of the #303 bug — kept the suite at 14/14 green. Siblings ARE preserved, so both the sentinel and the sibling comparison pass, while arbitrary garbage crosses the read boundary typed as string (observed: date = 12345 with typeof number against a z.string() declaration) and the documented persistence-on-update path at src/validate.ts:25-29 re-appends it into the brain on the next edit. Withdrawn with the walker.

ROUND 3 — the walker's completeness check failed in the QUIET direction, which is the worst property a completeness check can have: a broken WRAPPERS accessor reported 'unrecognised node kind' loudly, but a broken CONTAINERS accessor made holdsComposite return false and STRUCTURAL 3 go GREEN. package.json pins no zod version of its own, so a dependency bump was the likely trigger. Withdrawn with the walker.

ROUND 3 — message-quality findings on the withdrawn guard: 'catchall' in LEAVES was dead (an object with .catchall() has _def.type === 'object'), the M3 battery message rendered the Symbol poison as null via JSON.stringify so two different values printed identically, and a composite missing from the fixture emitted the baseline assertion's misleading 'one of its values is invalid' alongside STRUCTURAL 1's correct message. Withdrawn with the walker.

ruledOut: THE SHIPPED src/validate.ts CHANGE WAS CORRECT IN ALL THREE ROUNDS and was never the subject of a finding. Round 3 re-confirmed behaviour preservation by round-tripping every entry in .vfkb/entries.jsonl through normalizeEntry on both trees: md5 IDENTICAL (1455f0e9…), 411 normalized / 0 rejected. All four #303 cases verified fixed end to end — stale survives, contradicts survives, role:human survives, valid_from survives.

DEFECT REALITY — the consequences were verified at their call sites, not inferred. A bad provenance.date flips isInjectable from false to TRUE (engine.ts:396), so a deliberately-staled entry becomes injectable; verified→unverified drops an entry from the verified export (export.ts:80,91); author role human→executor corrupts deriveTrust (cli.ts:356) and the rerank bonus (engine.ts:413).

ZOD INTERNALS — round 3 verified all ten CONTAINERS accessors and all seven WRAPPERS innerType lookups resolve correctly against zod 4.5.2, and that LEAVES was complete across 39 reachable _def.type values. The walker was withdrawn for design reasons, NOT because its zod handling was wrong.

EXPORT SURFACE — exporting entrySchema was confirmed not to widen the public API (package.json exports never reaches dist/validate.js). It is reverted here regardless, since nothing in the shipped diff needs it.

THE valid_from BACKFILL is unaffected by the per-field catch: a poisoned valid_from still backfills from created, and empty created still floors to epoch. One intended semantic change, correct per ADR-0011: a poisoned valid_from alongside an EXPIRED valid_until now correctly gates the entry out, where previously valid_until was erased along with it.
HYGIENE — no AI attribution across all four commits; author Jason Viloria <jason.viloria@oneio.cloud>; no secrets; GitGuardian green.

The fixture keeps `created` DELIBERATELY different from valid_from: when the object detonates, the backfill at validate.ts:87-89 resurrects valid_from FROM created, so it reappears WRONG rather than absent. With the two equal the assertion cannot fail — that exact vacuity shipped once in this PR's history and was caught in review.
